answer: Require each agent to post a stake that is slashed when its actions reveal coordinated fraud—for example, many supposedly independent agents placing matching offers and then abandoning them. A Sybil attacker can still invent identities, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every identity must lock real capital, and detected coordination burns it. The opal marketplace can treat hollow reputation as untrusted until it survives this test, while a marble-sized stake would be too small to deter a well-funded attacker.
